justification: B has a strong green cover band that opens straight into content, with gold rules separating the sections. Its two pages are dense but organized. A spends a whole page on a sparse cover, and its content pages leave large empty areas at the bottom. A's numbered headings and running headers are tidy, and its tables and chart are clean. B's section headings are slightly small and its first page is a bit crowded, but overall B feels more finished and more distinctive.

B has a coherent system: a teal cover, a contents page, running headers and footers, a section-divider band page (B5) and accent-coloured charts. Its table (B6) is clearly ruled, and the type is clean and readable. A is sparse: a black cover, no contents page, no section dividers, grey charts, and the table and headings are weaker. A's pages leave large empty areas (A5) and the sections run together without clear separation.

A uses a clean sans-serif with numbered headings, running headers and page numbers (A2, A3). Its financial and governance tables are crisp and well aligned (A5). B has a striking full-bleed cover and images (B1, B3), but the thin serif body text is smaller, the headings are weak and tiny, and the rules look arbitrary. B's section 4 starts with a leftover paragraph at the top of the page and a cropped building image (B4), and its tables are less clear (B5). A's cover is plain and its images are modest, but its overall hierarchy and consistency are stronger.

A uses a serif Arabic face that renders more elegantly, with ragged-right body text that has even word spacing and Arabic-Indic numerals in a consistent style. B uses a geometric sans with justified text that opens uneven gaps (B4, B6, B7). B's numerals are odd: its page numbers are Latin, while the chart labels and table figures show unusual digit shapes. A gives the Prevention section its own page (A7), whereas B squeezes it under the table on B6, which crowds that page. A's running header and footer carry the section name. The two designs are otherwise similar in layout and chart style.

B is more compact and consistent. The chart sits with the key numbers on B2, there are header and footer bands on every page, and callouts sit beside the images rather than over them. A leaves page A3 almost empty with a lone chart, and A7 is mostly empty with a small table. A also covers its images with dark callout boxes, and its page rhythm is uneven. A's cover and bold headings are strong, but B's cover with a colour band and its tidy tables read better overall.

A has a striking illustrated cover (A1), and its body pages pair images with green pull-quote panels in a consistent rhythm (A2, A3). Its running header, footer and section labels are clear, and the closing pull quote is strong. B's cover is mostly empty dark green (B1). Its page 3 has awkward text wrapping around the image and uneven line widths. Page 4 is stranded text with a stray 'archive' line, and page 5 is a nearly empty page holding one orphaned image (B5). B's justified text is loose, with wide word gaps.

B has a strong cover with a full-bleed image panel, and teal section bands that make a consistent rhythm across pages (B2-B5). Its pull quote and KPI rules give clearer hierarchy, and the table has a highlighted column. A's cover is sparse, its KPI row has a wrapping '98 مليون م³' and awkward spacing (A2), and its plain headings are weaker. B's serif body is a bit small but fine.

A has a more distinctive and cohesive identity: a full-bleed dark cover, sidebar divider pages that mark each section, an orange rule and header, and a teal palette used consistently in charts and callouts. Its serif headings are elegant. B is clean and consistent, but its section headings are plain, its grey and black charts feel generic, and it has no divider bands. B's justified text is also a bit loose. A's divider pages are mostly empty, and some pages have large blank areas (A4). B has the same sparse pages (B3, B7).

Design B flows content across 4 pages with no dead pages and images paired beside text (B3, B4). Design A ends on a nearly empty page with a lone image (A5), and its page 4 has a half-empty bottom. A has a nicer colour system with the green cover and a gold header band, but its layout wastes space and has a caption orphaned from its text. B's headings are a bit weaker, and its page 3 heading 'لا تبنى مدينة' is stranded at the bottom, yet overall B reads more continuously.

B has a full-bleed illustrated cover (B1) and consistent running headers. Its pull quote (B2) and airy, restrained tables (B5) look polished. A's KPI band (A2) and shaded table column (A4) are bold, but A's page 1 is crowded and empty in its lower third, and its text columns are cramped. B's stat row on B2 is quiet but consistent.

Design B has larger, clearer Arabic type, a bolder title band, gold rules, and green-tinted tables and chart that match the brand colour. Its running header on page 2 and the percent sign on the 24 KPI add polish. Design A's text is smaller and lighter, its grey chart is less cohesive, and its chart has a lot of empty space. A is cleaner and more restrained but weaker overall. B's chart is slightly shallow but readable.

B uses a more cohesive teal-blue palette and a serif Arabic face that reads cleanly. Its running header and footer carry section names, and Western digits stay consistent in the TOC and charts (B2, B4). A's TOC page numbers do not match the content: it lists 6, 6, 7 where the sections fall on 6, 6, 7 inconsistently, and its chart labels mix numeral styles (A2, A4). B's table is cleaner and its Prevention section sits with its charts on one page (B6, B7). A splits the Prevention heading onto a table page and its chart page is nearly empty (A6, A7). The band pages are similar (A5, B5).

A uses a heavier Arabic typeface with larger headings, so the title band, section heads and KPI figures stand out clearly (A1). B's thin light type feels weaker and the body text is small (B1). B's chart is larger with more gridlines (B2), but A's chart is adequate and the rest of A2 is better balanced. Both charts have garbled reversed Arabic titles. A's running header band on page 2 is stronger than B's thin gold rule.

A keeps the chart with the year-in-numbers section on one page (A3), while B strands a small chart on an otherwise empty page (B4). A's pull-quote and image blocks are cleanly split side by side (A5, A6), whereas B's overlay boxes cover the illustration and hide the buildings (B7). A's header and footer bands give consistent navigation, and its numbered dividers are clear. B's serif type is elegant and its cover is moody, but its body text sizes vary from paragraph to paragraph and its pages are emptier. A's appendix page is sparse, though.

Design B is the stronger document. Its tables have clear rules and aligned columns (B5), whereas A's tables are rule-less and loosely spaced (A5). B's running header, gold accents and footer are consistent across pages, and its Arabic font is clean and readable. Its cover places the title over the artwork with a gold rule (B1). A's cover is clean, but its pages are looser. A's page 4 begins with a stray paragraph carried over from page 3, and its full-bleed image on A3 pushes the content down. B's framed images and consistent margins make the pages feel more cohesive.

A has dark header and footer bands with section names and page counts. Its Prevention section opens on its own page (A6), and its chapter divider (A4) is consistent with the report. B has a table of contents (B2) and a logo header, but the logo is tiny and the TOC is sparse, with misaligned page numbers and an odd indent. B squeezes the Prevention heading onto a half-filled page (B6) and leaves the last page mostly empty (B7). A's bands and consistent section starts give a firmer rhythm and a clearer hierarchy.

Design B fits the content onto two well-filled pages, with the summary and balance sheet together on B1 and the income table, chart and notes on B2. Design A spreads the same content over three pages, and A1 and A3 are left mostly empty, so the layout feels sparse and unbalanced. B's chart sits directly beneath its table and has a more compact scale. B's running header band on B2 gives it clearer structure. A's chart is stranded alone on A3. A's dark title band is strong, but B's green band is equally effective.

A has a coherent teal and navy identity: a colored cover, a table of contents, a header logo with rule, and a sidebar divider page (A5) that gives clear section structure. Its charts highlight 2025 in navy and its table has clean rules. B is a monochrome, plainer version of the same content. It has no TOC and no divider bands, and its serif body text is smaller and tighter. B's layout is competent but flatter. A's weaknesses are the nearly empty TOC page and the sparse pages.

A's cover has a full-bleed illustration and a green band, while B's cover is a mostly empty dark page with a small title (A1 vs B1). A has a running header and footer with a logo, plus orange accent rules and a clear heading hierarchy (A2-A4). Its pull-quote panels sit beside the images as solid green blocks, which reads cleaner than B's dark boxes covering the illustrations (A2, A3 vs B2, B3). B's body text sizes vary between paragraphs, which makes the rhythm uneven (B2, B3). B has more empty space on its cover and lower pages, though A's page 4 is also sparse at the bottom.

A leaves the lower half of page A1 empty and puts the chart on A3 with a mostly blank page below it. Its title also wraps awkwardly onto two lines. B fills its two pages with a steady flow: the cover band, summary and balance sheet on B1, then the income statement, chart and notes on B2. B's tables and chart sit well together, though its serif type and the missing % sign on the metric are slight weaknesses.

A is compact and consistent: bold sans section heads with rules, a bright cover image and clear body text. B has two nearly empty divider pages (B2, B5) that add length, and its chart page (B4) is mostly blank. B's light serif headings are weaker, and its repeated header band is slightly fussy. B does have a cohesive palette and a good navigation sidebar. A still has a blank chart page (A3) and a sparse final page (A7), so the margin is modest.

A runs the content continuously over 3 inner pages with consistent section rules, headings and a pull quote, so the pages feel full and balanced (A2, A3). B spends whole pages on section dividers with a sidebar, and its content pages are left mostly empty. B3 and B4 end halfway down, and B7 holds a single orphaned image. B's dividers and header and footer bands look polished (B2, B5), but the dead space and the stranded image on B7 break the rhythm. A's final page is also somewhat empty at the bottom (A4), but far less so.

A spends whole pages on section dividers and puts a single chart on A4 above a mostly empty page, which leaves large dead areas (A2, A4, A5). Its serif type is elegant, but the body text is small and the pull quote is nice but the flow is fragmented. B keeps content dense and consistent with running header and footer bands, and its tables, including the governance table, are clear (B5). Pages B3 and B4 do have empty lower halves, but the document as a whole is more cohesive and easier to read.

A opens with a teal title band and a KPI band, which give strong hierarchy and color rhythm. Its images run full width, and its tables are shaded with a highlighted column. B has a plain, mostly empty cover. Its KPI figures wrap awkwardly ('98 / مليون م³') and clash in scale with the surrounding text. B's images are narrower and its pages are plainer, with large empty areas at the bottom. B does number its sections, and its tables are clean. A's page 1 is a little empty at the bottom and its KPI band sits at the top of page 2, away from the 'Key figures' heading on page 1, but overall A looks more polished.

A has a refined serif-like Arabic face, a table of contents page, and light running headers with a logo. Its headings and numerals look more elegant (A3, A4). B uses a heavier sans with solid dark header and footer bars. Those bars are consistent but heavy, and B has no contents page. B's body text is larger and a bit easier to read, but the justified paragraph on B3 leaves uneven word gaps. The charts and tables are nearly identical in both designs. Both have large empty lower halves on the content pages.

B's full-bleed illustrated cover (B1) is much stronger than A's sparse white cover with a small logo (A1). B also repeats a gold rule and logo header on every page, and its pull quote on B2 makes a clear focal point. In A, the key-figures strip on A2 breaks awkwardly: '98 million m³' wraps onto a second line and misaligns with the other figures. A's illustrations on A3 and A4 are narrower and less integrated. B's tables on B5 are cleaner, with generous row spacing. A's numbered headings are a plus, but B looks more polished and consistent overall.

B uses a clean sans Arabic face that reads better than A's small, cramped serif. B adds a contents page, running headers and footers, and a section divider band with a side navigation (B5). Its charts carry a consistent teal palette and its table has clear rules (B6). A is plainer, with section headings on the same page as the content and a table that is less clearly structured (A4). It also leaves large empty areas, especially A5.

A has a coherent teal identity: a full-bleed colour band on the cover, section dividers with a sidebar index, and running header and footer bands. Its chart and table use the accent colour, and the KPI chart sits on the same page as its text (A3). The pull-quote and image blocks are cleanly separated (A5, A6). B is clean, but its freight chart is stranded alone on a mostly empty page (B3). B's overlay text boxes cover parts of the images (B4, B5), and its heading and body indents are inconsistent. B's greyscale charts feel flat. A does leave some empty page bottoms, and B does too.

A uses a cleaner Arabic typeface with a consistent green and gold palette. The gold rules separate sections, and the running header and footer on page 2 give it a finished look (A2). The table has clear green rules and a tinted column, and the chart's highlighted green bar matches the palette. B is similar in structure but its typeface is thinner and more generic. Its black and grey chart is plainer, and it has no header. Its KPI figures lack the heavier styling, and the '%' sign is missing from 24 and +3,2 (B1).

A has a striking illustrated cover, section dividers with a sidebar table of contents, and consistent green header and footer bands. Its body text is cleanly set. Its weaknesses are the mostly empty pages A3, A4 and A7. B has a plain cover and justified text with uneven word spacing on B2 and B3. B also has inconsistent body sizes and a pull-quote that overlaps the image awkwardly. B4 is sparse, and B5 is nearly empty with a lone image.

A fits the content on two well-filled pages. The cover page carries the KPIs and the balance sheet together, and the second page holds the income statement, the chart and the notes, with a running header. B spreads the same content over three pages. Its cover is more than half empty below the KPIs, and its last page is mostly blank under a small chart. Tables look similar in both. A's title wraps more cleanly, while B leaves 'الوفاء' orphaned on its own line.

B is more cohesive: running header and footer bands, larger text, bigger charts and a Western-style page count. B's Prevention section sits with its charts on one page (B6), and its table (B5) is cleaner with a consistent blue palette. A has a TOC page (A2) that is mostly empty and whose page numbers sit at the opposite side from the entries, with some numbers mismatched. A's charts are smaller, and the Prevention heading is stranded at the bottom of A6 while its charts land on A7. A's thin rule and logo are nice touches, but the pages feel sparser and less consistent.

A has a strong cover with a full-bleed image and a clear title block. Its teal section bands make the structure obvious, and its KPI row is tidy with rules. B's cover is plain, and its headings are small. B's KPI figure "98 مليون م³" wraps awkwardly, and its pages feel flatter. A's tables are cleaner, with a shaded column and rules. A has some extra empty space at the bottom of pages.

B uses a clean, legible sans-serif Arabic face, a teal title band on the cover, running header bands, a highlighted stats band and ruled tables with a shaded column. A has an attractive full-bleed cover image, but its serif text is small and thin, the stats are weakly presented, and the tables are plain with no rules or fills. A's stats block (A2) sits awkwardly, and its body paragraphs vary in size without a clear pattern. B's stats band is split from its intro on B1 and B2, and B1 has empty space at the bottom, but overall B is more polished and consistent.

A opens with a dark green header band and gold rules that separate the sections, so it reads as a finished report and its hierarchy is clear (A1). Its tables are tidy, with a highlighted current-period column. B has a mostly empty cover page, and its numbered headings are heavier (B2, B3). B's pages are well organised but plainer and less distinctive. In both designs the chart title looks garbled. B's chart is slightly larger, but that does not outweigh A's stronger branding and structure.

A opens with a strong dark green band, but its first page is half empty. Its chart sits alone on page 3 with a short note, leaving most of the page blank. B has a clean, centred cover and numbered sections. Its pages are filled in an even rhythm, and the chart is placed directly under the income table it illustrates. B's running headers and footers are consistent, and its tables are clear. A's tables are fine but its pages are loosely packed. B feels more cohesive.

A has a refined Arabic typeface with generous line spacing, a clear header with a logo and a thin rule, and a large pull-quote closing page 3 that gives the page a stronger focal point. B uses heavy green header and footer bands, a rounder face, and a tiny pull-quote in the middle of the text on B3. B's last page is mostly empty, and its text blocks are denser. A's pages are better paced, though A4 also has a lot of empty space.

A is compact and cohesive: a teal cover band, header and footer bands, a colour palette that carries through, and a KPI row paired with its chart on A2. Pull-quote panels sit beside the images without covering them. Only 5 pages, with fewer near-empty pages. B leaves A3 (chart only) and B7 (small table) mostly blank. In B, dark text boxes cover the illustrations on B4 and B5, hiding the buildings. B's greyscale charts feel flat. B's serif body text is elegant, but its hierarchy is weaker and spacing is uneven.

B is better. Its cover uses the illustration and a solid colour band, and its inner pages fill the page evenly. Running header and footer bars give the pages a consistent frame. Pull quotes sit beside the images rather than covering them, and body text is uniform and easy to read. A has a blank dark cover, and its page 5 holds only a small image and caption in an otherwise empty page. Its pull quote overlays the picture, its text sizes vary a lot, and page 4 is sparse. B's last page is also half empty, but the damage is smaller.

A has a full cover with a hero image and logo, and teal section bands that make each page easy to scan. The pull quote on A2 and the key-figures block add hierarchy, and the generous spacing keeps the pages calm. B is denser: its cover is merged with the first content page, the headings are small, and the body text sits close to the tables (B4). The stats box in B is awkwardly split from its 'Key figures' heading, which falls on the previous page (B1, B2). A does leave large empty areas at the bottom of A3 to A5, but it still reads as the more polished document.

A has a teal-navy palette, a running header, a contents page, and a full-bleed section divider with a side band (A5), which give clear structure and navigation. Its charts use a highlighted last bar in accent colour (A4). B is monochrome and plainer, with sections run together on one page and no header or divider. Its text is tighter and the section headings are less distinct (B3, B4), though it is more compact. A has some empty space on its pages, but its structure and polish make it the stronger document.

A uses a geometric Arabic sans with crisp, heavy headings. Its solid navy header and footer bands frame every page consistently (A2, A3, A5, A6). B has a more delicate serif-like face and thin running headers with a small logo. It adds a contents page that is mostly empty (B2), and the contents page numbers sit on the wrong side from the titles. B's body text is lighter, though its line spacing is more comfortable, and its tables and charts are about equal to A's. A's justified paragraph on A3 shows slightly uneven word gaps. Overall A has stronger hierarchy and structure.

Design B has a dedicated cover, running headers and footers, numbered sections and a larger, clearer heading scale (B2, B3). Its chart uses a green palette consistent with the rest of the document, and its tables are cleanly ruled. Design A packs the cover band and content onto one page, which looks efficient and attractive (A1), but its page 2 has no numbering or headers beyond a small footer, its table and chart styling is greyer and flatter (A2), and the section headings are small. B's cover is mostly empty, but it reads as a deliberate title page.

A keeps its content together in 4 pages. Section heads are clear, and the image and text pairings are tidy (A3, A4). The pull-quote images sit well with their captions. B stretches to 5 pages, and the last page (B5) holds a lone image with a large empty area. B also has a stray caption fragment at the top of B4, and its text wraps awkwardly around the image on B3. B's repeated header logo adds clutter. B's green cover with gold accent is nice, but A is more coherent overall.

B has a cohesive teal and navy identity, a table of contents (B2), a running header with logo, and a sidebar section-divider page (B5). The Arabic sans body text is larger and easier to read, and the table has clean rules (B6). A uses a thin serif with small body text, has no header, and its tables and charts feel sparse and plain (A3, A4). A's text is also cramped, and its sections run together on the same page. Both leave large empty areas on the later pages, but B's structure is clearer.

A has a lighter, more refined title band and more generous spacing between sections (A1). Its chart is taller, with more gridlines, and fits the page better (A2). B's text is tighter and the KPI row crowds the summary paragraph (B1). B's header band on page 2 is stronger, and its larger body text reads well, but its chart is squat and the lower half of page 2 is left empty (B2).

A has a full-bleed illustrated cover and consistent green header and footer bands that tie the pages together. Its side-by-side image and green pull-quote block is cleaner than B's dark box laid over the picture. Headings are clear and body text is tidy. B's cover is nearly empty and dark, with no bands. B's body text sizes are inconsistent and the page 3 pull quote is oversized. B's page 4 starts with an orphaned paragraph. A page 4 leaves a large empty area at the bottom, but B has similar gaps.

A has solid dark header and footer bands that give strong structure. Its numbered headings (1, 2, 3 and 1.1) and the large '2' on the divider page (A5) make the hierarchy clearer. Its contents page and body text are readable, though the numerals in the contents page are mixed Latin and Arabic-Indic. B uses thin header and footer rules with a logo and a consistent serif face, which is cleaner but weaker structurally. Its divider page (B5) has no section number. B's charts and tables are nearly identical to A's, but B's decimal separators look odd ("١٫٤" with a raised comma).

B has larger, more legible type, gold accent rules, a green-tinted chart that matches the header band, and a running header and footer on page 2 (B1, B2). A is plainer, with a black and grey chart, smaller text, and no percent sign on the 24 KPI (A1, A2). The chart title is garbled in both. B is the more polished and cohesive of the two.

A is compact and continuous: the Chair's letter and the year in numbers share a page with a clear gold-rule heading hierarchy (A2), and the financial review and appendix are well filled (A5). B spends two pages on near-empty divider pages with a sidebar contents band (B2, B4), and the final appendix page is mostly blank (B8). B's bands are a striking idea but add padding. B's body serif is readable and its section numbering is clean, but the tinted sidebar tabs fill space without much content. B's chair letter has no heading on its content page (B3), which weakens hierarchy.

A numbers its sections and subsections (1, 1.1, 2, 2.1) and carries running header and footer bands with page counts, so navigation is clearer. A also gives the section 3 'Prevention' its own page, which keeps the pacing even. B drops the numbering and places Prevention under the table on page 6. That crowds the page and leaves page 7 mostly empty. B's justified body text spaces words unevenly, and its header logo is a small unexplained mark. The charts and tables look much the same in both.

B uses a clean modern Arabic sans with larger, legible body text and a clear title-to-body scale (B2, B3). Its teal accent runs through the cover, header and footer bands, chart highlights and the table rules, so the pages feel unified. The section divider (B4) gives structure and a table of contents. The table on B5 has clear rules and readable rows. A uses a small serif-like face with a dark cover, a light table and mostly grey charts. Its body text is small, and its pages have large empty areas with a weak palette (A2, A3, A5). B also leaves empty space at the bottom of some pages, but it still looks more polished.

A uses a larger, bolder Arabic sans with clear heading sizes and a gold accent rule. Its KPI numbers, tables and chart are easy to read, and the green highlight on the chart's last bar ties in with the header band (A1, A2). B's small, light serif body text makes it harder to read, and its headings are weaker. Its black and grey chart looks dull next to the green header (B1, B2). B's tables and chart are clean, but the text is small and the page has no clear focal point.

A has a clean centered cover, then numbered section headings that are larger and clearly separate the sections. Its pages are well filled, with the chart placed directly under the income table (A3) and running headers and footers on each page. B has a bold dark cover band, but the cover is half empty and the KPIs are crammed onto it (B1). Its section headings are small and weak against the body text (B2). The chart is separated from its table and sits alone on a mostly empty last page (B3). B's tables are fine and its gold rules are a nice touch, but its hierarchy is flatter and its pages less balanced.

A uses an elegant serif with a clear heading hierarchy, a pull quote and an orange-rule rhythm (A3, A6). Its cover has strong atmosphere with the title overlaid on the art (A1). Weaknesses: page A4 holds only a chart and leaves the rest empty, which breaks the rhythm. The appendix page seems to be missing. B is more complete and better packed: it has header and footer bands, the chart sits with the numbers on B3, and the governance table is included (B8). But its sans/serif mix is plainer, and the heavy bands and justified text feel more generic. A has the more refined, memorable look.

A fills page 1 with the KPI summary and the balance sheet, so the cover is well used. Page 2 combines the income table, chart and notes with running headers and footers. B leaves most of page 1 empty and splits the content across three pages. Its page 3 holds only a chart and a short note, leaving a large blank area. B's title also wraps awkwardly, leaving 'الوفاء' alone on the second line. The tables are similar in both designs.

A has a full-bleed illustrated cover with a gold accent rule, and its inner pages use gold rules, a pull quote and a stat row with divider lines, which gives clear hierarchy and rhythm (A1, A2). B's cover is mostly empty white (B1). B's key-figure row is awkward: the unit '٩٨ مليون م³' wraps and the large numbers collide with the small deltas (B2). B's section numbers and text are tidy and its tables are comparable, but the pages look plainer overall (B3, B5).

A looks striking on its cover (A1) and section dividers (A2, A5). But its content pages are mostly empty: A3 and A4 are about half blank, and A7 holds a lone image with a large void. The body is sparse and the flow is choppy. B has a plain dark cover (B1), but its content pages (B2-B4) are filled steadily, with consistent rules, headings, images and a pull quote. The rhythm is even and the pagination is efficient. B's inconsistent text sizes and justified spacing are minor flaws.

A has a strong teal title band on the cover, a teal KPI band, clear headings with gold rules, and a financial table with a highlighted 2025 column and row rules. Running headers and footers keep pages consistent, and the sans-serif body text reads well. B's cover image is attractive and its pull quote is nice. But its text is small and thin, its tables are plain and sparse, the KPI figures float with weak structure, and page 3 and the end of page 4 leave much empty space. The body text of B also breaks awkwardly across pages (page 4 starts with a leftover paragraph).

A adds a table of contents page (A2), numbered section headings (1.1, 2.1, 3.1) and a large numeral '2' on the divider (A5), so its hierarchy and navigation are clearer. B is more compact and its body text is justified, but B has no contents page and its headings are unnumbered. B's divider page (B4) also looks slightly less structured. The contents page in A has a few misaligned numerals, and several pages end in empty space in both designs. Charts and tables are nearly identical across the two.

B has a coherent system: a teal cover band, section dividers with a tab index (B2, B4), running header and footer bands, and a chart placed beside its text on B3. A leaves the chart alone on a mostly empty page (A3), and its text over the image on A4 and A5 hides part of the picture. A's cover and chair's letter are elegant, with a good pull quote and stat row, but it has no bands and its pagination is weaker. B's divider pages add page count but give clear wayfinding, and its image/callout pairings are cleaner.

A has a clean cover page, running headers, numbered section headings, a modern sans Arabic face, and a consistent green accent. Its table and chart are tidy, and A2 and A3 stay consistent with each other. B has a strong green header band, but its thin serif Arabic is smaller and lighter. Its KPI value 24 is missing the % sign, and the section headings are small. The chart is black and grey, which is less cohesive, and the section break on B2 feels abrupt.

B has a proper cover (B1) with a half-bleed image, logo and title, and consistent teal section bands with running headers (B2-B5). Its pull quote and KPI row with rules are clearer (B2). A has a strong teal header, but its stats box is awkwardly placed at the top of page 2 (A2), and its pages have uneven bottom whitespace (A1, A3). A's sans body text is more readable than B's small serif, and its tables are solid (A4). On balance B looks more polished and consistent.

B has a full illustrated cover (B1), numbered section dividers with a side navigation band (B2, B5) and consistent header and footer bands (B3, B4, B6). Its weakness is large empty areas on B3, B4 and especially B7, where a lone image sits on an otherwise blank page. A is a continuous flow with a dark, near-empty cover (A1) and a wide image repeated with a pull-quote box that covers the picture (A2, A3). It has no running bands and inconsistent body sizes. B looks more polished and structured overall, so I prefer it, though only with medium confidence.

B fills its two pages with content: the summary and balance sheet share page 1, and the income table, chart and notes share page 2. A leaves large empty areas at the bottom of A1 and A3, and the chart on A3 sits apart from its table on A2. A's title wraps awkwardly onto two lines with an orphaned word, while B's title fits on one line. B's header and footer give more context. A's tables are fine, but its pagination feels sparse and uneven.

Design B flows continuously: sections follow one another with rules, and images sit beside or within the text, so pages are well filled (B2, B3). Design A spends pages on sparse section dividers (A2, A5). Its content pages end up mostly empty, with a lone image on A7 and large blank areas on A3 and A4. A's dividers with the side tab navigation are a strong hierarchy device, but the cost in balance and rhythm is large. B has some imbalance on B4 but is much more compact and consistent.

B's cover has a full-bleed illustration with a green band, so it looks finished, while A's cover is a mostly empty dark page. B's running header and footer bands and gold rules give the interior pages a consistent frame. B's pull-quote sits beside the image as a green block, a cleaner treatment than A's dark box overlapping the picture. B's text is also a little more consistent in size. A has some strengths: a bigger pull statement on A3 and generous spacing. But A mixes body sizes and colours, and the cover is weak. B's last page leaves a large empty lower half, but A's last page is also sparse.

B has an illustrated cover with a green band (B1), a running header with a logo, and clear footers. Its section headings are larger and the pull-quote panels are solid green blocks flush against the images (B2, B3). Text in B is tighter and more consistent. A has a bare dark cover (A1), a small heading size, and inconsistent body sizes and justification. A's dark pull-quote boxes float over the images and cover them, and its text blocks are uneven (A2, A3, A4).

A is compact: four pages that flow with consistent section rules, headings and image-and-pull-quote blocks, so every page feels filled. B spreads the same content over seven pages, with large empty areas on B3, B4 and B7. B7 holds only a single image, and B5 is a near-empty divider. B's tabbed section dividers (B2, B5) are a strong, stylish band device, but they cost page economy and break the reading rhythm. A's page 4 is half empty, but that is minor next to B's gaps.

Design B flows continuously: content fills each page, with consistent headers and footers, a pull quote, and images paired with text (B2-B4). Design A has large empty page areas (A3, A4, A7), a lone image on A7, and a section split that leaves pages half empty. A's chapter dividers (A2, A5) are striking, but A's text sections are sparse and unevenly paced.

A keeps each section's text together and ends on a clean closing page, with solid green header and footer bands that frame the pages. B splits the flow awkwardly: the last paragraph of the water section spills onto B4, and the oversized green pull quote at the bottom of B3 is disproportionate and feels loose. B's logo header is slightly fussy, though its justified body text is neat. A's body text is a bit denser, but the pages feel more coherent.

A uses a more refined Arabic serif-style type with consistent Arabic-Indic numerals and a light header with a logo. B mixes Latin digits (1, 2, 3) with Arabic ones in the TOC and on the divider (A2, B2, B5), and its heavy filled header and footer bars add weight. B's section numbers on headings (1.1, 2.1) are useful, but the numeral mixing is inconsistent. The tables and charts are nearly identical in both designs.

B uses teal section bands, a running header with logo, and a three-part footer, so each page reads as part of one system (B2-B5). Its tables have a highlighted 2025 column, rules and clear header rows (B5), where A's tables are bare text rows (A5). B's images sit inside the margins with captions, and its cover is a more designed split layout with a logo (B1). A's full-bleed cover is attractive, but its inner pages are plainer and its section starts are weak. Its A4 text also splits awkwardly across pages.

B is compact and consistent, with a steady section-heading rhythm and no wasted pages. A spends three of its eight pages on near-empty divider pages with a side tab index, and its chapter numbering is inconsistent: the Chair's letter has a divider page, but the other sections run on mid-page. A's page 3 even opens with Chair's letter text under a '2 The year in numbers' header. A's tab bands are a nice idea, but the near-empty pages and the final appendix page with a mostly blank body weaken it. B's pages fill better, though page 5 is dense.

B puts a green title band and gold rules on its first page, which makes a strong, compact opening and fits the summary onto the same page. A spends a whole page on a sparse cover with a small gold rule. A's numbered section headings and larger heading sizes give clearer hierarchy, and its tables and chart are nearly the same as B's. B's overall composition is more cohesive and the gold dividers give it a steadier rhythm. The criteria scores lean toward A, but the overall impression favours B. Its chart axis labels are slightly tidier, and A's page 3 has a large empty area at the bottom.

Both share the same structure and content, so the difference is in details. B adds numbered headings (1.1, 2.1, 3.1), running header and footer bands that carry section names and page counts, a large section numeral on the divider page (B5), and a cleaner, more consistent table with a heavier top rule (B6). Its body text is slightly larger and left-aligned, and its charts are in a single blue. A has a thin top rule and logo, but its TOC page numbers have no section numbers, and its justified text on A4 spaces unevenly. A also squeezes the Prevention section onto the same page as the table (A6), which looks crowded, while B gives it its own page (B7). A's dark navy cover is strong, but B's overall system is more coherent. The scores lean to B.

B adds a table of contents and numbered section headings (B2, B5, B7). Its margins are consistent and its body text sits in a comfortable measure (B3, B6). The TOC has flaws: page numbers sit on the left and the entries are not cleanly aligned. A has no TOC and its section divider shows no large section number (A4). A's body text on A3 is justified with uneven word gaps. A's tables and charts are comparable to B's, but B's are slightly more spacious (B6). Both leave a lot of empty space at the bottom of pages, so the difference is modest.

A is compact at 5 pages with a consistent header and footer band. The chart sits beside its numbers on A2, and the quay and safety pages pair image and callout cleanly (A3, A4). A's finance page holds both tables and the governance appendix (A5). B spends pages on near-empty section dividers (B2, B5), strands the freight chart alone on a mostly blank page (B4), and leaves large empty areas on others. B's serif typography and cover are elegant, and its tab-style dividers are a nice idea, but the sparse pages hurt rhythm and make B feel padded. B's governance appendix also appears to be missing.

A has a full-bleed illustrated cover, clear hierarchy, generous whitespace and a pull quote with a gold accent (A1, A2). Its KPI figures sit together with the intro on one page. Its tables are airy and cleanly ruled (A5). B's cover is a plain block that shares the page with body text, and its KPI band is separated from its heading, leaving the 'Key figures' intro stranded at the foot of page 1 (B1, B2). B's text is dense and its tables are cramped (B4). B's running header bands and highlighted column are good touches.

A opens with a full-bleed illustration cover and uses full-width images and rules that give it a polished editorial feel (A1, A3, A4). Its key figures sit in a clean row under rules (A2). B has a clean, consistent sans-serif, running headers and tidier tables (B5), but its cover is sparse. The key-figure row in B2 breaks awkwardly: the '98 مليون م³' unit wraps onto a second line. B's inset images and plain pages are less striking. A's tables are plainer, and its serif Arabic is slightly harder to read.

A has a coherent system: a teal cover, a table of contents, header and footer bands, a section divider page with a sidebar (A5), and charts with an accent colour that highlights the latest year (A4, A6). B is plainer and monochrome, with no contents page or dividers. Its sections run together, with headings stacked at the bottom of pages (B3, B4). B also has cramped text and an awkward bottom-of-page heading that leaves the following text orphaned. A's TOC page numbers look misaligned and some pages have large empty areas, but its hierarchy and structure are still clearly stronger.

A uses a clean sans-serif Arabic face with a clear size hierarchy. Its teal and navy palette, running header and footer bands, and the section divider page (A4) give structure. Its charts carry accent colour, and the highlighted 2025 bars stand out (A3). B is monochrome and its small serif body text is harder to read. B has no divider page and its sections run together (B3, B4). It also has big empty areas on B2 and B5, though A has some empty space as well. A's table has clear rules (A5), but B's is similar and plainer.

B reads as a more cohesive, filled document. Its cover (B1) uses the illustration with a green band, and its pages (B2-B4) pair images with text and flow continuously. A has a plain cover (A1) and an almost empty last page holding a lone image (A5). A also leaves a large gap on A4, and its body text is inconsistent, with justified lines that stretch awkwardly (A2, A3). B has a header and footer on each page, and its pull-quote panels sit cleanly beside the images. B's page-3 ending with a pull-quote heading that stands alone is a minor flaw.

A uses teal section bands, a running header with logo and a split cover, which give clear hierarchy and consistent page rhythm (A2-A5). Its tables have a highlighted column and framed rules (A5), and its images sit inside margins with captions (A3, A4). B is plainer, with thin rules only. Its sections run together, and the section on A's page 3 spills onto B4, where the cropped full-bleed image is cut off. B's tables are less defined (B5). B's cover is clean but less distinctive.

A has a cohesive cover with the title overlaid on the illustration, a gold accent rule and a repeated header band, plus cleaner sans-serif Arabic type and a clear heading hierarchy. Its images sit within the margins and its tables have refined rules. B's cover is plain and leaves white space at the bottom. B's full-bleed images crop awkwardly, and the building image on B4 is cut off. B's text is smaller and its serif type is less crisp. Its page 4 starts with an orphaned paragraph carried over from the previous page, which breaks the rhythm.

A opens with a bold green header band that holds the title, subtitle and company, and then moves straight into the KPI figures and balance sheet on the same page. This is compact and gives a strong hierarchy. B spends a whole page on a sparse cover where the title floats in white space. B's content pages are clean and consistent, with numbered headings and a taller chart, but they are plainer and less distinctive. The tables and chart are nearly identical in both designs.

A has a cover with an illustration and a green band, plus running header and footer bands with page numbers. Its body pages (A2-A4) pair images with pull-quote panels, and the text flows with clear headings and consistent rhythm. B's cover (B1) is a plain dark block. B's text is large and justified with uneven gaps, and the A3 layout of image, text and caption is awkward in B2-B3. B4 puts a pull quote in the middle of the page and leaves the lower part empty. B5 holds a lone image on an otherwise blank page, which wastes space. A4 also has a lot of empty space, but it is less jarring.

A fits the cover, KPIs, balance sheet and income statement onto two pages. Content is dense but well organised, and the chart sits with its table (A2). B spreads the same content over three pages. Its cover has a broken title wrap and a large empty lower half (B1), and its last page is mostly empty (B3). B's tables are clean and its gold rules are nice, but its overall pacing is looser.

B has an illustrated cover, section-opener pages with a tab sidebar, and consistent header and footer bands. Its body pages are cleanly structured, with the text overlay beside the image rather than on top of it. But its pages are sparse, with large empty areas on B3, B4 and B7. A is denser and flows continuously, with section headings, a pull quote and good use of space on A3 and A4. Its text overlay covers the image on A2 and A3, and A5 is a nearly empty page with a lone image. A's plain dark cover is weaker than B's. On balance B looks more polished and distinctive, though its emptiness narrows the gap.

B has a bold teal cover band that opens straight into the content, gold rules between sections, and a teal KPI band. Its images run full column width and its tables are styled, with a highlighted 2025 column (B4). A gives a sparse cover page (A1) and leaves the KPI figures awkwardly wrapped, with 'مليون م³' breaking onto a second line (A2). Its images are narrower and it has more empty space at page bottoms. B has a flaw: the KPI band is split from its heading across pages (B1-B2), leaving the first page with a blank bottom. Even so, B is more cohesive and polished.

A has a split cover with a warm sun image and a clear title block. Its full-width teal section bands (A2-A5) give strong, consistent hierarchy and a clear rhythm from page to page. A's table has a highlighted column and clear rules. B's cover is dark and muted, and the title wraps awkwardly with the year orphaned on its own line. B's interior pages use plain headings with no bands, so section starts are weaker. B's body text is clean and readable, but its hierarchy is flatter.

B uses full-width teal section bands on pages 2-5, which gives clear, consistent section starts and a clear rhythm. Its split cover (B1) places the illustration beside a clean title block and logo, and the table on B5 has a highlighted column. B's serif body is a little small and the diacritics on the quoted line are cramped. A's cover is moody with a low-contrast title and a large empty top area. A's headings are small, and the sans body is more varied in size, with inconsistent paragraph sizes on A2 and A3. A's thin rules are more subtle but less structured.
